$comment: Typechecking only. Nothing here is built: Prime loads the harness .ts files
through jiti and the conformance suite runs them under Node's native type
stripping, so the emitted output would never be used and `noEmit` makes
that explicit rather than leaving a dist/ nobody reads.
`erasableSyntaxOnly` is the load-bearing option. Node's type stripping
erases types without transforming, so enums, parameter properties and
namespaces are syntax errors at runtime rather than downlevelled. Without
this flag tsc would happily accept code that Node refuses to run, which is
precisely the class of error a typecheck is supposed to catch here.
`verbatimModuleSyntax` for the same reason: type-only imports must be
written as such, because the stripper does not do import elision.
